findings.evidence: Lines 55–85 permit any additive integral carrier, while `Hom` at lines 116–122 stores only a rational map and its induced complex filtration condition; tensoring torsion with `ℚ` or `ℂ` annihilates it.
findings.fix: Require the integral carrier to be a genuine lattice (at least `Module.Free ℤ intCarrier`, with the appropriate finiteness condition) or formulate the rational object directly from its rational-to-complex comparison so invisible torsion is not stored.
findings.issue: `intCarrier` is only an `AddCommGroup`, so arbitrary torsion can be added without changing either base change, the Hodge structure, or any morphism; the bundle therefore contains free data invisible to the category.

findings.evidence: The functor definitions are exposed at lines 431 and 468; their object/map equations are exported with `[simp]` at lines 444, 448, 481, and 486.
findings.fix: Remove both `@[expose]` annotations and keep consumers on the four public characteristic lemmas.
findings.issue: `rational` and `complex` (also line 468) expose their complete functor bodies even though their object and map behavior is already provided by `rational_obj`, `rational_map_hom`, `complex_obj`, and `complex_map_hom`.

summary: The object bundle retains invisible torsion data, and both realization functors unnecessarily expose their implementations despite having characteristic lemmas.
